global_issues.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield Hits 5.1%, Stocks Slide on Rate Fears
global_issues.note: Yield spike to 5.11% on 2026-09-23 is confirmed, and yields remain elevated (~5.17-5.18% as of Sept 25-27). But the 'stocks slide' framing is stale: markets rallied after this — Nasdaq hit a record +2% on Sept 20, S&P 500 rose 0.51% on Sept 25, and futures were higher heading into Sept 28 as oil/yields cooled. The briefing's risk-off tone no longer matches price action.

global_issues.title: Oil Falls to Two-Week Lows Near $89 Despite Iran Shipping Disruptions
global_issues.note: WTI is trading ~$92-93 as of Sept 27, not near $89 (Brent ~$104-105). More importantly, the 'Iran-related disruptions'/'Trump-Iran talks' framing severely understates reality: this is an active shooting war (Day 209+ of the '2026 Iran War'), with a US naval blockade of Iran, missile/tanker strikes traded in the last 24-48 hours (IRGC fired ballistic missiles at a US carrier group), and Iran issuing a 5-day ultimatum at the UN for a ceasefire. This is a live military conflict, not diplomatic talks with 'mixed signals.'

grok_report.summary: The 10Y yield spike and chip-bill gridlock are accurately reported, and watchlist price levels (NVDA, CRWD) check out against real data. The main problems are the oil/Iran item, which downplays an active shooting war and naval blockade as mild 'shipping disruptions' and has WTI off by several dollars, and a market mood/headline that was accurate on Sept 23 but is now stale given the subsequent rally into record highs and firmer futures heading into Sept 28.
